title: K-flat complexes of module objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, with the small pro-étale site and universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object [pur713-def-ring-object] of $\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$. Write $\mathcal B=\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(X_{\Proet})$ for the category of module objects [pur713-def-modules]. Complexes are unbounded $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complexes, with cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; acyclic means that every cohomology object is zero. The direct-sum total tensor, formed using the relative tensor product of [pur713-def-relative-tensor], is
$$
(P\otimes_{\mathcal R}N)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_{\mathcal R}N^q,
\qquad
 d|_{(p,q)}=d_P^p\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_N^q.
$$
The two displayed components land in the $(p+1,q)$ and $(p,q+1)$ summands, respectively. A complex $P$ is K-flat if $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}N$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $N$ of $\mathcal B$. A K-flat resolution of $M$ is a quasi-isomorphism $P\to M$ with $P$ K-flat. Functorial K-flat resolutions exist: there is a functor $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal B)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $q:Q\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$ such that each $Q(M)$ is K-flat and each $q_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the existing abelian-group closed symmetric monoidal structure and its flat separator Z, hence its functorial flat cover (WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.RingObjects.Ab). The essentially small pro-etale site then inherits the Grothendieck abelian closed sheaf tensor and functorial flat cover. These are the existing source instances, with the stated u+1 coefficient universe.

proof.text: For the commutative ring object R, apply the existing Mod Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric relative-tensor and functorial-flat-resolution instances. The closedness of the recorded relative tensor gives colimit preservation in each factor, and its monoidal preadditivity is the existing module-object instance. Thus B = Mod(Sh(X_proet,Ab),R) satisfies all hypotheses of kFlat_derivability. Its flat cover is free R-module on a flat cover of the underlying abelian sheaf, followed by the action.

proof.text: Choose the already constructed flat cover LeftResolution Lambda from HasFunctorialFlatResolution B. Apply kFlat_derivability to its underlying endofunctor, augmentation, flatness certificates and epi components. Obtain Q and q : Q => id with IsKFlatForTotalTensor values and quasi-isomorphic augmentation components. This choice occurs only inside an existence proof; it defines no object of the library from an unproved existence theorem.

For acyclic N, the zero map N -> 0 is a quasi-isomorphism: quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt' identifies this degreewise with exactness of N because the zero complex is exact. The left half of hQ(M) makes tensorHom (identity Q(M)) (N -> 0) a quasi-isomorphism. The binary total-tensor functor T = ((curriedTensor B).map2CochainComplex).obj (Q.obj M) is additive, by the proved source bifunctor API, hence maps the zero complex to a zero object. Its target is therefore acyclic. Applying quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt' in every degree now proves the source tensorObj (Q.obj M) N acyclic, exactly IsKFlatModuleObject X R (Q.obj M). Pair this with hq(M). This uses only binary total tensors, with no monoidal structure on complexes.
